title: Probability with Possibility Diagrams
topic: Probability - Possibility Diagrams and Sample Spaces
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.explanation: Each die has 6 outcomes. Total outcomes = 6 x 6 = 36. A possibility diagram would show a 6 by 6 grid.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 2?
questions.explanation: Only one outcome gives sum 2: (1,1). P(sum 2) = 1/36.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 12?
questions.explanation: Only one outcome gives sum 12: (6,6). P(sum 12) = 1/36.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. Which sum has the highest probability?
questions.explanation: Sum of 7 has the most combinations: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) = 6 ways. All other sums have fewer ways.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is greater than 10?
Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the product of the two numbers is 12?
Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that both dice show the same number?
A fair coin is tossed 3 times. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.explanation: Each toss has 2 outcomes. Total = 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 outcomes.

questions.question: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads?
questions.explanation: Outcomes with exactly 2 heads: HHT, HTH, THH = 3 outcomes. P = 3/8.

questions.question: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. What is the probability of getting at least 2 heads?
questions.explanation: At least 2 heads means 2 or 3 heads. 2 heads: HHT, HTH, THH = 3. 3 heads: HHH = 1. Total = 4. P = 4/8 = 1/2.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the difference between the two numbers is 1?
A spinner has sections 1, 2, 3 and another spinner has sections A, B. How many outcomes are in the combined sample space?
questions.explanation: First spinner: 3 outcomes. Second spinner: 2 outcomes. Total = 3 x 2 = 6 outcomes: (1,A), (1,B), (2,A), (2,B), (3,A), (3,B).

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the first die shows a larger number than the second die?
questions.explanation: Count outcomes where first > second. By symmetry, P(first > second) = P(second > first). With 6 ties, remaining 30 split equally: 15/36.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that at least one die shows a 6?
Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is even?
questions.explanation: Sum is even when both odd or both even. P(both odd) = 3/6 x 3/6 = 9/36. P(both even) = 3/6 x 3/6 = 9/36. Total = 18/36 = 1/2.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is odd?
questions.explanation: Sum is odd when one die is odd and the other is even. P(odd sum) = 1 - P(even sum) = 1 - 1/2 = 1/2.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is a prime number?
Two fair four-sided dice (numbered 1-4) are rolled. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.explanation: Each die has 4 outcomes. Total = 4 x 4 = 16 outcomes.

questions.question: Two fair four-sided dice (numbered 1-4) are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 5?
Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that exactly one die shows an even number?
questions.explanation: Exactly one even means (odd, even) or (even, odd). P = 3/6 x 3/6 + 3/6 x 3/6 = 9/36 + 9/36 = 18/36 = 1/2.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that neither die shows a 1?
questions.explanation: P(not 1) = 5/6 for each die. P(neither shows 1) = 5/6 x 5/6 = 25/36.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. Given that the sum is 8, how many possible outcomes are there?
A fair coin and a fair die are tossed together. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.explanation: Coin: 2 outcomes. Die: 6 outcomes. Total = 2 x 6 = 12 outcomes.

questions.question: A fair coin and a fair die are tossed together. What is the probability of getting a tail and a number greater than 4?
Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is at most 4?
Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the product is odd?
questions.explanation: Product is odd only when both numbers are odd. Odd numbers: 1, 3, 5. P(both odd) = 3/6 x 3/6 = 9/36 = 1/4.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the larger of the two numbers shown is 4?
A bag contains 2 red and 3 blue balls. Two balls are drawn with replacement. What is the total number of outcomes?
questions.explanation: With replacement, each draw has 5 outcomes (2 red + 3 blue). Total outcomes = 5 x 5 = 25.

questions.question: Using the bag from the previous question (2 red, 3 blue), what is the probability of drawing 2 different colours with replacement?
questions.explanation: Different colours: (red, blue) or (blue, red). P(R then B) = 2/5 x 3/5 = 6/25. P(B then R) = 3/5 x 2/5 = 6/25. Total = 12/25.
